Activate a policy version to a canary scope (subset of the fleet) before

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Activate a policy version to a CANARY scope (a subset of the fleet) rather
than fleet-wide. The version is served only to in-scope nodes/tenants (or a
percentage slice) while a metric-based evaluator watches the success window;
it then either promotes fleet-wide, auto-rolls back on breach, or pauses on
an inconclusive signal. Additive to the Phase-K activation surface.

post.summary: Promote a baked, within-threshold canary to fleet-wide enforcement.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Promote a baked (within-threshold) canary to fleet-wide. Fails unless the
canary is promote-eligible (ACTIVE and its success window has elapsed within
threshold). On success the canaried version becomes the active version of its
policy set fleet-wide and the canary moves to PROMOTED.

post.summary:
Stage 2: authorize and, when allowed, mint a short-lived native-access
contract (restricted role + scoped DSN + RLS session variables).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
`GetNativeAccess` runs the same `Authorize` decision and, when allowed,
mints a short-lived contract for the caller to talk to the backend
directly: a restricted role, a scoped DSN, and the exact set of
`app.current_*` session variables the SDK must `SET LOCAL` so the
broker-generated RLS policies still apply. UDB stays the source of the
authorization decision; the native grant only carries it forward.

post.summary: Stage 2: return a signed policy bundle for local SDK authorization caches.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
`GetPolicyBundle` serializes the live authorization snapshot (policies,
role bindings, relationship tuples) and signs it so an SDK can cache it
and answer `can()` locally without a round-trip, while still being able
to verify the bundle was issued by UDB and has not expired.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

v1ApiKeyOwnerType.description:
- API_KEY_OWNER_TYPE_INTEGRATION: External system integration.
 - API_KEY_OWNER_TYPE_CICD: CI/CD pipeline
 - API_KEY_OWNER_TYPE_ANALYTICS: Read-only analytics / BI tool
 - API_KEY_OWNER_TYPE_TENANT: Tenant-scoped integration key
 - API_KEY_OWNER_TYPE_PROJECT: Project/application-scoped key
v1ApiKeyOwnerType.title: Owner types — who this key belongs to

v1Asset.description: Asset wraps a storage File and tracks its processing lifecycle.

v1AssuranceLevel.description:
Normalized authentication assurance level derived from IdP auth-context /
MFA claims. Higher ordinal == stronger assurance. Authz policies (Phase K)
may require a minimum assurance level; the value is stamped onto sessions and
audit records so a decision can be correlated to how the subject authenticated.

 - ASSURANCE_LEVEL_NONE: unauthenticated / anonymous
 - ASSURANCE_LEVEL_LOW: single factor, unverified context
 - ASSURANCE_LEVEL_SINGLE_FACTOR: single factor, verified (pwd / IdP w/o MFA)
 - ASSURANCE_LEVEL_MULTI_FACTOR: MFA asserted by IdP (amr/acr)
 - ASSURANCE_LEVEL_HARDWARE: phishing-resistant / hardware-backed (WebAuthn, smartcard)

v1CanaryScopeKind.description:
How a canary's exposure is scoped before fleet-wide promotion. A canary
version is only served to in-scope nodes/tenants (or a percentage slice)
while it bakes; the metric evaluator then either promotes it fleet-wide or
auto-rolls it back.

 - CANARY_SCOPE_KIND_NODE: scope_values is an explicit list of control-plane node ids.
 - CANARY_SCOPE_KIND_TENANT: scope_values is an explicit list of tenant ids.
 - CANARY_SCOPE_KIND_PERCENT: scope_values[0] is an integer 1..=100 percentage; membership is a stable
hash bucket of the node/tenant id.

v1CanaryState.description:
Lifecycle state of a progressive-rollout canary.

 - CANARY_STATE_ACTIVE: Baking: the version is live for the in-scope subset and the evaluator is
watching the success metric over the success window.
 - CANARY_STATE_PROMOTED: The success window passed within threshold and the canary was promoted
fleet-wide (the version is now the active version of its policy set).
 - CANARY_STATE_ROLLED_BACK: A metric breach inside the window triggered an automatic rollback to the
policy set's prior (rollback) version.
 - CANARY_STATE_PAUSED: The signal was inconclusive (insufficient samples): the canary is held —
neither promoted nor rolled back — pending more data / operator action.

Sessions and token families bind to a device; revoking a device blocks future

digest (STORAGE_ONLY); IP is stored masked and the user agent only as a hash.

Id of the PASSWORD_RESET OTP issued (empty when the account is unknown; the

Dev-only echo of the plaintext PASSWORD_RESET OTP code, populated ONLY when the

Plaintext codes, returned exactly ONCE. Only keyed hashes are stored; any

v1GovernanceActor.description:
The governance actor whose authorization is checked under
`native.authz.governance` for every governance mutation. The AUTHORITATIVE
caller identity and scopes come from the verified claim (the bearer token),
NOT from this message. The `subject` / `scopes` / `roles` fields here are
accepted ONLY as cross-tenant-admin / impersonation TARGET hints; they never
grant capability and are ignored for authorizing the caller. The
`break_glass*` fields below are the only authoritative body fields on this
message (a short-TTL emergency bypass with a recorded reason).

audiencesJson.description: JSON array of accepted token audiences.

v1IdentityProvider.description:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IdentityProvider — Tenant-scoped SSO/identity provider configuration.

One row per (tenant, provider). The kind determines which fields are
meaningful: OIDC uses issuer/jwks_url/client_ids/audiences; SAML uses
entity_id/saml_metadata_url. claim/group/jit mappings are JSON-encoded
policies consumed by the IdP runtime. RLS scopes rows to the current tenant.

Migration order 10 — after the authn tables so external identities can FK to
users; before SCIM directory state.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kind of identity provider configured for a tenant.

 - IDP_KIND_OIDC: OpenID Connect (discovery + JWKS)
 - IDP_KIND_SAML: SAML 2.0 web SSO
 - IDP_KIND_LDAP: LDAP / Active Directory bind

The minted native-access contract. Present only when the embedded

`GetNativeAccess` runs the same `Authorize` decision and, when allowed,
mints a short-lived contract for the caller to talk to the backend
directly: a restricted role, a scoped DSN, and the exact set of
`app.current_*` session variables the SDK must `SET LOCAL` so the
broker-generated RLS policies still apply. UDB stays the source of the
authorization decision; the native grant only carries it forward.

v1PipelineDefinition.description: PipelineDefinition is a reusable, versioned processing-pipeline template.

v1PolicyApproval.description:
A single reviewer/approver decision recorded against a PolicyDraft (Phase K
draft/approval workflow). Separation of duties is enforced in the handler: the
draft author cannot record an APPROVE decision (author != approver). Each row
is one actor's REVIEWER/APPROVER decision with a mandatory reason.

⚠️ CROSS-SESSION: field set reconstructed to EXACTLY match the governance
session's `governance_store.rs::load_approval` struct literal (the source of
truth). The governance-session owner should confirm / restore their canonical
file.

version.description: The promoted version, present once the draft is approved.

v1PolicyBundleRequest.description:
`GetPolicyBundle` serializes the live authorization snapshot (policies,
role bindings, relationship tuples) and signs it so an SDK can cache it
and answer `can()` locally without a round-trip, while still being able
to verify the bundle was issued by UDB and has not expired.
v1PolicyBundleRequest.title: ── Stage 2: signed policy bundles for local SDK authorization caches ───────

scopeValues.description:
For NODE/TENANT: the list of in-scope ids. For PERCENT: a single-element
list whose value is the integer percentage (1..=100).

successWindowSecs.description: The evaluator waits at least this long before declaring success.

metricThreshold.description:
The success metric breach threshold (e.g. fractional authz deny/error rate).
A measured value strictly greater than this inside the window auto-rolls back.

minSamples.description:
Minimum sample count required for a conclusive evaluation. Below this the
canary PAUSES instead of promoting or rolling back.

rollbackVersionId.description:
The version a rollback restores to (the policy set's active version at
canary-creation time). Recorded so auto-rollback is deterministic.

outcomeReason.description: Why the canary left ACTIVE (breach reason, 'promoted', 'inconclusive').

v1PolicyCanary.description:
A progressive-rollout canary: a `PolicyVersion` exposed to a SUBSET of the
fleet (by node id, tenant id, or percentage) and watched by a metric-based
evaluator before fleet-wide promotion. If the success metric breaches
`metric_threshold` within `success_window_secs`, the canary auto-rolls back
to the policy set's prior version BEFORE fleet-wide impact; if the window
passes within threshold it becomes promote-eligible; if samples are
insufficient it pauses. Every state transition is audited.

v1PolicyDocument.description:
A candidate policy document the governance APIs operate on (drafts and
simulations). Unifies the full field richness of CreatePolicyRule and
PutAuthzPolicy (role, purpose, relationship, priority, required scopes,
conditions, tenant, project, domain) so every governed surface is parity.

v1PolicyDraft.description:
An editable, in-progress policy change set under review (Phase K draft/approval
workflow). Holds the proposed policies/tuples as JSON; when approved it is
promoted into an immutable numbered PolicyVersion. Drafts never affect live
decisions.

⚠️ CROSS-SESSION: field set reconstructed to EXACTLY match the governance
session's `governance_store.rs::load_draft` struct literal (the source of
truth). The governance-session owner should still confirm this is their
intended schema / restore their canonical file.

document.description: Document parsed back from the stored draft (convenience).

v1PolicyRule.description: Managed permission rule mapped into UDB authorization policy rows.

v1PolicySet.description:
A governed collection of policy versions. Each tenant/project/name names one
policy set; its `active_version_id` points at the currently-enforced
`PolicyVersion`, and `rollback_version_id` records the version a rollback
restored to. Drafts are created against a policy set and only take effect
once a version is activated (Phase K governance workflow).

sourceDraftId.description: The PolicyDraft this version was promoted from, if any.

v1PolicyVersion.description:
An immutable, numbered version of a policy set. A `PolicyDraft` that passes
review is promoted into a `PolicyVersion` whose frozen `payload_json`
(policies + role bindings + relationship tuples) is what
`ActivatePolicyVersion` loads into the live authorization snapshot. Drafts
remain editable; versions never change once created — they only transition
state (draft -> pending_review -> approved -> active -> superseded /
rejected / rolled_back). `revision` provides optimistic concurrency over the
version's state transitions; `content_hash` detects no-op promotions.

v1PolicyVersionState.description: Lifecycle state of a governed policy version (Phase K draft/approval workflow).

mappedPrincipalJson.description: Fully-resolved principal fields as JSON for inspection.

roles.description: Roles granted (only roles explicitly present in the mapping).

unmappedGroups.description: Input groups that matched no mapping entry (granted nothing).

v1PromoteCanaryRequest.description:
Promote a baked (within-threshold) canary to fleet-wide. Fails unless the
canary is promote-eligible (ACTIVE and its success window has elapsed within
threshold). On success the canaried version becomes the active version of its
policy set fleet-wide and the canary moves to PROMOTED.

v1ProviderHealth.description:
Health of a provider's discovery + key material.

 - PROVIDER_HEALTH_DEGRADED: last refresh failed, serving cached keys
 - PROVIDER_HEALTH_UNREACHABLE: discovery/JWKS unreachable, no usable keys

v1ReconciliationAnalyticsSummary.description:
Daily reconciliation/conflict roll-up for projections, imports, replicated
stores, and project-defined resolution workflows.

latencyMs.description: Raw observation for a single request (will be aggregated hourly).

refreshToken.description:
Rotated refresh token (token-family credential). Issued on every successful
refresh: the presented refresh token is single-use and is invalidated as the
new one is minted (atomic rotation). Empty when the caller refreshed with a
legacy server-side session id rather than a token-family credential.

isPublic.description: Optional initial visibility; absent defaults to private (false).

sizeBytes.description: Declared upload size in bytes, used for the pre-upload tenant quota check.

expiresAt.description:
Unix-seconds expiry of the presigned PUT `upload_url`; 0 when no URL was
minted (metadata-only mode / presign error). Lets the client know when the

v1RelationshipTuple.description: ReBAC tuple scoped to a tenant/project domain.

v1Resource.description: One versioned resource on the wire (a single ControlPlaneResource projection).

v1ResourceType.description:
- RESOURCE_TYPE_ROUTING_POLICY: Request routing / backend selection policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_METHOD_SECURITY_POLICY: Per-RPC method-security policy (the proto endpoint_security map).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RLS_TENANT_POLICY: Row-level-security / tenant isolation policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_NATIVE_SERVICE_ENABLEMENT: Which native control-plane services are enabled on a node.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_BACKEND_TARGET_DEFINITION: Backend target/cluster definitions — the "definitions" that routing and
RLS policies reference. Pushed BEFORE the referencing policies.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ResourceType — the kinds of control-plane configuration a node can subscribe
to in the xDS-style versioned distribution stream. "Definition" resources
(backend targets) MUST be pushed before referencing policies so a referencing
policy is never applied before its target exists (make-before-break).
